title: Powers of a real number below one tend to zero
statement: Let $b\in\mathbf R$ satisfy $0\le b<1$. Then the sequence $(b^n)_{n\in\mathbf N}$ converges to $0$ as $n\to\infty$. For $b>0$, the notation $b^n$ is the positive-real power of [def-weil-real-power] at the natural exponent $n$; for $b=0$, put $0^0=1$ and $0^n=0$ for $n\ge1$.

source.place: Proof, last sentence: geometric decay of the normalized energy ratios; Mathlib/Analysis/SpecificLimits/Basic.lean:188-192
